English: Ember Stand
A humble, makeshift fire pit, tended by the clans elders, marking the first Indo-Aryan sacred fire on the steppes. Used for daily rituals and as a gathering point.
Torch Post
A set of upright torches encircling the main camp, symbolizing the Indo-Aryan journey and illuminating the sacred grounds each evening.
Fire Pit
A larger, stone-lined pit for ritual offerings, drawing in the faithful and strengthening communal ties around the sacred Indo-Aryan flame.
Flame Pavilion
A tented, wind-guarded structure for sacred fire rites and gatherings, attended by priests and clan leaders for grander ceremonies.
Priests Room
A dedicated enclosure for the clans fire priests, storing ritual implements and providing a sanctum for Indo-Aryan spiritual guidance.
Altar Chamber
A portable wooden altar, richly decorated, for major sacrifices and clan-wide rituals, reinforcing Indo-Aryan faith on the move.
Sanctified Hall
A semi-permanent hall adorned with banners and icons, where Indo-Aryan fire rituals and councils are held, fostering unity and respect.
Holy Fire Pavilion
A grand, timber-framed ritual hall with an ornate hearth, attended by Indo-Aryan priests for legendary ceremonies and oaths.
Blessed Sanctuary
A revered sanctuary of stone and wood, home to the Indo-Aryan sacred fire, drawing pilgrims and increasing the clans spiritual prestige.
Indo-Aryan Fire Temple
A monumental, stone-built fire temple, seat of Indo-Aryan faith on the steppes
French: a center of unity, learning, and devotion for generations.
